text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - Britain's leading share index powered to its second highest close in a broad-based rally that continued to feed off a favourable outlook for British interest rates and sterling. The FTSE 100 closed at 5075.8, up 43.9 points, or 0.87 percent.

FRANKFURT - German shares posted gains on modest volumes, heartened by an upbeat close on Wall Street overnight, the stable dollar and the Bundesbank's reassuring decision not to raise a key interest rate. The DAX-30 index closed at 4,363.09, up 29.96 points, or 0.69 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,377.51, up 44.36 points, or 1.02 percent.
PARIS - French shares closed up half a percentage point, supported by dollar firmness, traders said. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,998.57, up 15.13 points, or 0.51 percent.
ZURICH - Insecurity about further developments in U.S. and German interest rates led Swiss shares to a lower close. The Swiss market index closed at 5,808.4, down 17.2 points, or 0.30 percent.

MILAN, Aug 12 - Italian stocks closed higher after the Bundesbank set a repo tender at an unchanged fixed rate which settled worries over German interest rates and supported by the firmer trend in early Wall Street trading.

AMSTERDAM - Dutch shares closed with modest gains, braking a fall which had lopped almost 40 points off the AEX index in the two sessions following Thursday's record close of 1,011. The AEX index closed at 978.40, up 5.33 points, or 0.55 percent.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks recovered modestly from the previous day's nearly four percent plunge in the benchmark index, as stability in the dollar and U.S. stocks prompted investors to bargain-hunt blue-chip exporter issues that had been hit hard on Monday, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 19099.11, up 274.93 points, or 1.46 percent.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended weak, reversing gains made earlier in the day, as a rising U.S. long bond yield and an increase in mortgage lending rates by two major banks prompted a slide in property shares. The Hang Seng index closed at 16383.41, down 77.06 points, or 0.47 percent.

SYDNEY - The Australian stock market fell away at the close to end the day near its lows after opening firmer in line with a stronger Wall St. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2650.5, down 16.7 points, or 0.63 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares finished off highs, failing to react positively to a better June producer price inflation and dragged lower by De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd's results which dealers described as "dissapointing." The All-share index closed at 7579.9, down 3.2 points, or 0.04 percent. The All Gold index closed at 1017.1, up 0.8 points, or 0.08 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 9267.7, up 28.3 points, or 0.31 percent.
